title: VPC networking: automation for subnet/NAT/endpoint provisioning + active health checks
creator: Luca Rivera
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module and orchestration pattern to provision VPC networking for Private deployments with explicit support for: subnet groups (public/private/isolated), NAT Gateway vs NAT Instance selection, Internet Gateway attachment, interface and gateway VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, KMS, Secrets Manager), route table wiring, and a lightweight active health-checking mechanism that validates route reachability, endpoint DNS resolution, and egress paths post-apply. The module should enable safe in-place upgrades, drift detection remediation hooks, and clear outputs for Console/ops consumption.
background: Current private deployment IaC work has several ad-hoc TF modules and scripts. Past tickets (listed in dependencies) consolidated VPC structure but lacked an automated verification step and safe upgrade story. We need a single source module that teams can consume for Dedicated and Private deployments which also gives the Console runtime deterministic network metadata and health signals.
scope: Create terraform module 'redwood_vpc_network' (registry-style), implement optional submodules for endpoints and nat, provide wrapper examples for private deployments, add a TF plan/lint/gate CI job, and deliver a small AWS Lambda-based health-checker (or container task) that runs post-deploy and reports to Console metrics/logs. Include migration docs and runbooks for existing stacks.
out_of_scope: Rewriting existing customer networks, multi-cloud (only AWS for initial rollout), deep packet inspection, or full CNI plugin changes.
acceptance_criteria: Module can create VPC with configurable CIDR, 3 AZ subnet groups (public/private/isolated) via simple variables
Option to choose NAT Gateway (managed) or NAT Instance with IAM role for smaller customers
VPC endpoints for S3 and ECR created as interface/gateway based on recommended defaults and overridable
Route tables wired correctly for public/private subnets and an explicit route to IGW/NAT
Post-apply health-check job runs and reports: DNS resolution for endpoints, TCP connect to endpoint ENIs, successful S3 Put/Get via VPC endpoint
Module exposes outputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids_by_role, nat_gateway_ids, endpoint_ids, route_table_ids, and a health_check_status URL/ARN
TF module passes CI: terraform fmt, validate, plan with no diffs on idempotent apply, and a smoke test that deploys into a test account and validates checks
Migration guide provided for existing stacks with step-by-step plan to adopt new module with zero downtime
Security review completed and KMS/Secrets Manager access scoped according to least privilege
design_decisions: Use modular structure: core VPC + subnets, endpoints submodule, nat submodule, health-checker as optional submodule
Default to NAT Gateway for reliability; allow NAT Instance for cost-sensitive small stacks
Prefer Gateway endpoints for S3, Interface endpoints for ECR/KMS/SecretsManager to align with AWS best practices
Health-checker implemented as a small Lambda container that runs a predefined test matrix and emits metrics to CloudWatch and a webhook for Console ingestion
Expose flags for IPv6 enablement but ship IPv6 disabled by default for this sprint
Idempotency: avoid random-generated names where possible; rely on TF computed names for stable resources to enable safe in-place upgrades
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: NAT Instance option may encourage deprecated patterns and increase maintenance. Mitigation: mark NAT Instance as p2 path, document security/patching responsibilities, and default to NAT Gateway
Risk: Creating interface endpoints increases ENI quotas in small accounts. Mitigation: provide a quota check in preflight and recommend consolidated endpoints or endpoint services where appropriate
Risk: Health-checker false positives due to transient network issues. Mitigation: implement retry/backoff and multi-check logic before marking failure and post incidents to an escalation runbook
Risk: Drift remediation could make destructive changes. Mitigation: only offer remediation hooks as opt-in and surface planned changes in Console before apply
implementation_plan: Week 1: module skeleton + core VPC/subnet resources + unit examples. Week 2: endpoints & NAT submodules, output wiring, and basic examples. Week 3: CI jobs, health-checker prototype, test account smoke tests. Week 4: security review, migration guide, docs, and internal rollout to Solutions Engineering for validation.
ci_and_testing: Add terraform-lint and checkov to pipeline, create a 'networking-smoke' GitHub Actions workflow that spins up the module in a dedicated test account, runs health-checker, and tears down. Add nightly drift detection job that runs terraform plan against a sample management stack and alerts on unexpected diffs.
